plan.topic: Orforglipron (Foundayo) vs the semaglutide pill head to head: ACHIEVE-3 in adults with type 2 diabetes
plan.angle: Did orforglipron beat the semaglutide pill in type 2 diabetes? In ACHIEVE-3 (52 weeks, adults with T2D on metformin), Lilly reported that A1C fell by 2.2 points on orforglipron 36 mg vs 1.4 on oral semaglutide 14 mg (Rybelsus), and weight fell by 9.2% vs 5.3%. Orforglipron has no food or water timing rules; the semaglutide pill does ('follow your label'). Dated status: orforglipron (Foundayo) is approved for weight management (Apr 1, 2026) but not yet for type 2 diabetes as of Oct 2026. Common side effects are GI (nausea, diarrhea). Don't switch on your own. Prescriber line.
plan.working_title: Orforglipron vs Semaglutide Pill: Who Lost More in Type 2 Diabetes? #shorts
plan.why: A rising 'did X beat Y?' story about two named drugs people already search for. The pill Short format works (53 views, 52 reach), and the comparison is a real randomized head-to-head. | fact-check: Verified via Lilly's ACHIEVE-3 release: 52 weeks, n=1,698, adults with T2D on metformin, 4 arms (orforglipron 12 and 36 mg; oral semaglutide 7 and 14 mg). A1C −1.9% / −2.2% vs −1.1% / −1.4%. Weight −9.2% (36 mg) vs −5.3% (oral semaglutide 14 mg). Credit as 'Lilly reported' unless a peer-reviewed paper is cited. Needed changes: (1) Label status. Foundayo is approved (Apr 1, 2026) for chronic weight management only. Lilly planned a T2D submission by end of Q2 2026. As of the latest sources I found, the T2D indication is NOT confirmed approved, so say 'not yet approved for type 2 diabetes as of Oct 2026 (submitted, per Lilly)' unless the FDA label shows otherwise. Don't imply it's a T2D option today. (2) Drop the indirect 25 mg comparison: it's a crowded number and a scope risk (the playbook warns about crowded numbers). (3) The Wegovy pill (approved Dec 22, 2025) is semaglutide 25 mg for weight, a different product and dose from the 14 mg Rybelsus-type arm in the trial. Call the comparator 'oral semaglutide 14 mg (the diabetes pill, Rybelsus)', not 'the Wegovy pill'. (4) A1C units are percentage points. Include one GI line, no verdict on which is better for you, and no switching advice. Lead with A1C, the primary endpoint, and frame weight as a secondary endpoint.

package.title: Orforglipron vs oral semaglutide: type 2 diabetes result #shorts
package.description:
ACHIEVE-3 (Lilly, 52 wks, ~1,700 adults with type 2 diabetes not controlled on metformin): orforglipron 36mg vs oral semaglutide 14mg — A1C -2.2 vs -1.4 pts, weight -9.2% vs -5.3% (Lilly-reported, if taken as directed).
About 10% vs 5% stopped for side effects (mostly GI, like nausea); oral semaglutide has food/water timing rules, orforglipron doesn't.
As of Oct 2026: orforglipron (Foundayo) is US-approved for weight management in adults with obesity, or overweight with a weight-related condition; type 2 diabetes use submitted, not yet approved. UK authorised both in August 2026.

This content is for educational purposes only and is not medical advice. Don't switch or stop your medicines on your own; talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether it's right for you.

social.instagram_caption:
Pill vs pill: who came out ahead in type 2 diabetes?

In Lilly's ACHIEVE-3 trial — 52 weeks, ~1,700 adults with type 2 diabetes not controlled on metformin — orforglipron (36mg) and oral semaglutide (14mg) went head to head:
🔹 A1C: down 2.2 points vs 1.4 points
🔹 Weight: down 9.2% vs 5.3%
🔹 Both as reported by Lilly, if taken as directed

The catch: oral semaglutide comes with food/water timing rules; orforglipron doesn't. Side effects were mostly GI, like nausea, and about 10% stopped orforglipron for side effects vs 5% for oral semaglutide.

As of Oct 2026: orforglipron (Foundayo) is approved in the US for weight management in adults with obesity, or overweight with a weight-related condition. Its use for type 2 diabetes has been submitted but isn't approved yet. The UK authorised both uses in August 2026.

Save this for your next conversation with your doctor about GLP-1 options.

A one-word re-hook ("Weight?") leads to the secondary endpoint. Then the practical catch (timing rules), the side-effect trade-off (stopping for side effects), a dated US and UK status, and a scoped verdict that loops back to "who won?" before the prescriber line.

factcheck.summary: I checked every number and status against primary sources, and all of them are right. On ACHIEVE-3, Lilly's press release (Sept 17, 2025) matches the script: 1,698 adults with type 2 diabetes not controlled on metformin, a 52-week open-label trial with 4 arms, the 'if taken as directed' (efficacy estimand) caveat, A1C −2.2 vs −1.4, body weight −9.2% vs −5.3% (36 mg vs 14 mg), stopping for side effects 9.7% vs 4.9%, and mostly mild-to-moderate gut side effects. The timing rules are right too: the Rybelsus/oral semaglutide label (revised Jan 30, 2026) says to take it with up to 4 oz of water and wait 30 minutes, and Lilly and the MHRA both say orforglipron has no food or water limits. The US status checks out: FDA approved Foundayo for chronic weight management on Apr 1, 2026, and the type 2 diabetes submission is confirmed in Lilly's Q2 2026 8-K (Aug 5, 2026), with no FDA decision found as of October 2026. The UK status checks out: the MHRA authorised it on Aug 10, 2026 for both weight and type 2 diabetes, and it isn't on the NHS yet (NICE review). The script credits the numbers to Lilly, names the funder, keeps the dose arms and estimand, mentions side effects, scopes the verdict and includes the prescriber and don't-switch lines. Only minor wording fixes remain.
